_metadata.description: Reviewed GHOST-SUSPECT findings from verify_backed_studies_citations.py --strict. A suspect blocks the release gate until it is reviewed here with a rationale that states why the live PubMed record does support the entry. Removing an entry re-arms the gate for that citation.

reviewed.live_title: An Extract of Glycyrrhiza glabra (GutGard) Alleviates Symptoms of Functional Dyspepsia
reviewed.rationale: False positive of the word-overlap heuristic, not a wrong-topic citation. The entry is Deglycyrrhizinated Licorice and its own notes cite this PMID for exactly this claim: 'The strongest modern trials are on the standardized GutGard extract for functional dyspepsia'. Glycyrrhiza glabra is licorice; the heuristic compares the live title against the stored ingredient words 'deglycyrrhizinated' and 'glycyrrhizin', which the botanical binomial does not string-match. Topic, extract name and indication all agree.

reviewed.live_title: Bioavailable turmeric extract for knee osteoarthritis: a randomized, non-inferiority trial versus paracetamol
reviewed.rationale: False positive of the title-only word-overlap heuristic. The live PubMed abstract's Methods section explicitly identifies the tested intervention as BCM-95 500 mg twice daily. This entry is scoped to the BCM-95/CurcuGreen formulation and explicitly disclaims evidence for the finished Life Extension retail product, so the PMID supports the authored formulation-level claim.

Primary PubMed identifies this as the retraction of lutein/zeaxanthin adolescent-myopia review PMID41573009 (DOI10.18240/ijo.2026.02.21). The corrected entry cites the notice only to exclude that original from affirmative evidence. Remaining PMID28661438 concerns a macular-carotenoid combination in 48 young adults, not isolated lutein or adolescent myopia prevention. A generic notice title is a title-heuristic miss; no affirmative credit or whole-record clearance is granted.

Provenance-only correction notice, not an efficacy source. Live NIH PubMed identifies35917215 as the ErratumFor34415830 PQQ disodium cognitive trial, DOI10.1080/27697061.2022.2099711. The generic title has no ingredient word, causing a title-overlap false positive. The PQQ record explicitly retains scoring_eligible=false because correctedTable4content remains unread; this acknowledgment verifies the correction link only and does not qualify original numbers, efficacy or safety.

reviewed.live_title: Effect of SKI 306X, a new herbal anti-arthritic agent, in patients with osteoarthritis of the knee: a double-blind placebo controlled study.
reviewed.rationale: The pending synthesis context cites this solely as a source-bibliography pointer. Live PubMed verifies SKI306X is a three-herb mixture, not glucosamine. Its doses/results must not qualify glucosamine or establish component quantities. The context is scoring_eligible=false; the former included_study_pmids designation was removed from these new, unapproved facts and all bibliography IDs retained as limitations. This acknowledgment verifies bibliographic identity only, not ingredient efficacy or a completed source assessment.

reviewed.live_title: Subacute Ingestion of Caffeine and Oolong Tea Increases Fat Oxidation without Affecting Energy Expenditure and Sleep Architecture: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blinded Cross-Over Trial.
reviewed.rationale: The pending source context cites this only as a source-bibliography pointer, not an independently qualifying theanine trial. Live PubMed names oolong tea/caffeine and fat oxidation; no isolated theanine exposure or cognitive benefit is established. The context remains scoring_eligible=false. Bibliographic citation is not proof of inclusion in a specific outcome pool, exact preparation, efficacy or dose; all pointers are retained with that limitation.

reviewed.live_title: Discrepancies in publications related to HMB-FA and ATP supplementation.
reviewed.rationale: Live PubMed and the full letter identify concerns about the shared HMB-FA/ATP trial family NCT01508338, including apparent shared placebo data and reporting inconsistencies. The original authors replied in PMID29209404 and contested the interpretation; that reply does not establish efficacy or resolve the clinical assessment. The HMB record cites this letter only as a limitation in scoring-ineligible study contexts. This acknowledgment is for source identity and caution provenance, not affirmative benefit credit or clinician approval.

reviewed.live_title: Oligofructose decreases serum lipopolysaccharide and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 in adults with overweight/obesity.
reviewed.rationale: Primary PubMed content verifies an oligofructose secondary biomarker analysis of a prior randomized placebo-controlled trial (21 g/day,12 weeks,37 participants with available samples). The inspected inulin-type-fructan synthesis includes this publication; oligofructose wording causes the generic ingredient-word heuristic to miss the correspondence. This is included-publication provenance only, not an independent participant cohort, ingredient-wide efficacy, universal inulin dose threshold or accepted product claim. Preserve null IL-6,TNF-alpha,MCP-1,adiponectin and resistin findings and the pending source context/eligibility holds. No clinical approval or safety clearance is added.
reviewed.reviewed_by: Codex primary NIH content and included-study-table verification
